entries.subject: ESO eso1537a
entries.finding: The star formation region Messier 17: B, V, R and H-alpha; 4000 × 3738 px over 35.44 × 33.12 arcmin. The file's embedded sky tags, used as they are: 0.5316 arcsec per pixel, north 0.0° left of vertical, the frame's centre at 275.2630836°, -16.1874792°. Not measured against Gaia here.

entries.subject: The shape of the Omega Nebula
entries.finding: The picture is flat. Depth needs the nebula's shape as a paper gives it; none was found for this star-forming region on 2026-10-03.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper prints a three-dimensional shape of the nebula.

entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The photograph first kept its stars, which stood on the nebula's plane whatever their own distances. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them and keeps the nebula's structure. The glow of the brightest stars remains. A second pass over a quarter-size copy takes saturated stars, but on this picture it also took real nebula, so it is not used. The galaxies' glow fill, which needs a star table, erased nebula around the stars that light it and is not used on nebulae.
